html:
The Günün a küna, also called the northern Tehuelche, were a hunting people of northern Patagonia and the southern Pampas of Argentina, between the Colorado and Chubut rivers. Günün a atük is the name of their land.

They hunted guanaco and rhea and gathered plants, living in skin tents and moving across the plains. After horses spread south in the 1600s they became horsemen and traded with the Spanish frontier. Mapuche groups moving east across the Andes in the 1700s and 1800s mixed with them, and the Conquest of the Desert by the Argentine army in 1878 to 1885 ended their independence. Their language, Gününa yajüch, died out in the 1900s. Their neighbours were the Aónikenk to the south and the Mapuche to the west.
